open_errors.issue: Rohan says there were no wardens on Shilak before the Closing Law. Ch14 makes his grandfather a warden of the Shilak post the winter before the law, and the founder Saro was a warden 300 winters ago. The line undercuts two series secrets (S3, S4).
open_errors.fix: Make the pre-law wardens keepers of the cairns who stopped no one.

patches.find: Before the Closing Law there were no wardens on Shilak. The passes were open in winter to anyone who could pay the road.
patches.replace: Before the Closing Law the wardens on Shilak kept the cairns and stopped no one. The passes were open in winter to anyone who could pay the road.

open_errors.issue: Meera tells Rohan she is 'not looking for something to hold on to', then calls it 'partly a lie'. A moment later she shows him her hands and says they are warm. A lie to a bound partner always costs heat, so this waives the cost.
open_errors.fix: Have her correct an incomplete statement instead of admitting a lie.

patches.find: "That's partly a lie. I'll start again."
patches.replace: "That isn't the whole of it. I'll start again."

open_errors.issue: In ch6 Rohan remembers Meera stating the promise rule 'among the rules, in the middle'. Her three rules in ch4 never mention promises.
open_errors.fix: Add the promise rule to rule two, the middle rule.

patches.find: "Kills the liar." She said it as flatly as she had said the odds on the gully.
patches.replace: "Kills the liar. And a promise made on this rope is a contract. Break it while we're bound and it strikes you like a great lie." She said it as flatly as she had said the odds on the gully.

open_errors.issue: Varun is said to have had 'two years of Rohan's temper'. Ch16 and ch17 say Rohan has known Varun for ten years and Varun held his horse when he was newly made captain.

patches.find: He looked up with the warm, lopsided smile that had got him through the officers' mess and two years of Rohan's temper.
patches.replace: He looked up with the warm, lopsided smile that had got him through the officers' mess and ten years of Rohan's temper.

open_errors.issue: Rohan says the carved hands are the same size. Ch32 makes it a key clue that the same carving shows one broad worker's hand and one long narrow hand.
open_errors.fix: Make the waystone carving too worn to compare.

patches.find: "The hands are the same size," he said. "No rank. No sword."
patches.replace: "The hands are worn too smooth to tell apart," he said. "No rank. No sword."

open_errors.issue: The Rope-Hut is barely one body-length long and the rope is eight arm-spans, so Meera cannot stop three steps short of the doorway. The limit she meets is the tree, ten paces outside.

patches.find: If he stayed on the dirt by the chulha, she stopped three steps short of the doorway.
patches.replace: If he stayed on the dirt by the chulha, she stopped three steps short of the tree.

open_errors.issue: Rohan makes flat statements of intent to his bound partner and then does not carry them out. In ch12 he says 'I will not be dragged' and is dragged. In ch17 he says 'I will take the door' and does not. Elsewhere 'I will not' hums as a promise (ch21), and breaking one would strike him as a great lie.
open_errors.fix: Soften both lines so they are wishes or requests, not statements of intent.

patches.find: "I will take the door as well. I will kick the drift clear and test the sill before you put a foot on it."
patches.replace: "Let me take the door as well. Let me kick the drift clear and test the sill before you put a foot on it."

open_errors.issue: Meera stripped the juniper sprig above the Rope-Hut door into the steam pot in ch11, and ch31 says the nail is bare. Ch15 still shows the sprig above the door.
open_errors.fix: Show the bare nail instead of the sprig.

patches.find: When the door of the Rope-Hut came out of the whiteness it was dark already, and the juniper sprig above it was stiff with ice.
patches.replace: When the door of the Rope-Hut came out of the whiteness it was dark already, and the bare nail above it was furred with ice.

open_errors.issue: The text says 'The hut had no stones to ring'. The Rope-Hut is built of stacked stone, and its wall stones hum at true words in ch10 and ch11.
open_errors.fix: Say that the wall stones stayed silent.

patches.find: The hut had no stones to ring.
patches.replace: The stones in the wall kept silent.

open_errors.issue: Meera says 'You said twelve paces back' about Varun lagging. Rohan never gave that figure; in ch3 Varun simply dropped back to fix a strap.

patches.find: "And he lagged. You said twelve paces back."
patches.replace: "And he lagged. He dropped back for a strap just before it went."

open_errors.issue: Ch17 says that for ten days Rohan took the downhill place on the rope and went first through every door. In fact he walked in her steps behind her (ch3, ch4, ch7) and she entered the hut first (ch8).
open_errors.fix: Make it a habit he kept reaching for and she kept stopping.

patches.find: For ten days he had taken the downhill place on the rope and gone first through every door, and she had let him, with a look and nothing more.
patches.replace: For ten days he had reached for the downhill place on the rope and the first step through every door, and she had turned him back, with a look and nothing more.

patches.find: Behind. Uphill. For ten days he had taken the downhill place on the rope, and she had put up with it.
patches.replace: Behind. Uphill. For ten days he had kept reaching for the downhill place on the rope, and she had put up with it.

open_errors.issue: Meera lists 'the weaver' in the first redbark wave. Hira the weaver was refused a course in ch18.
open_errors.fix: Replace the weaver with Bholu's mother, who did get a course.

patches.find: The first wave is the three youngest and the weaver.
patches.replace: The first wave is the three youngest and Bholu's mother.

open_errors.issue: Ch22 offers Hakam's three-fingered hand as proof of what a great lie does. Ch26 says Hakam's fingers were 'the mountain's doing', in contrast to Meera's own lie.
open_errors.fix: Make Hakam's loss frost, compared with what a great lie does.

patches.find: She had seen Hakam's hand in the yard of Kothi Shilak, three fingers where there should have been five.
patches.replace: It did what the frost had done to Hakam's hand in the yard of Kothi Shilak: three fingers where there should have been five.

open_errors.issue: In ch18 Kamla's two are judged 'gone too deep' and get no course, and all eighteen courses are assigned. In ch23 the same children sit up to play the knot game, and three spare doses appear for them without explanation.
open_errors.fix: Source the doses from Sunni's unfinished course and note that the children rallied.

patches.find: "Three doses," she said. "The Dev boy's father. Kamla's two. After that I brew walnut leaf and I swear at it."
patches.replace: "Three doses, what Sunni never finished," she said. "The Dev boy's father. Kamla's two, who came up out of that sleep on walnut leaf and spite. After that I brew walnut leaf and I swear at it."

open_errors.issue: Meera tells the buyer that nine packets crossed Shilak. Twelve crossed; three were ruined on the Goat's Teeth.
open_errors.fix: Say twelve crossed and nine came through sound.

patches.find: "Nine packets of redbark crossed Shilak in my pack," she said. "They're in Ranu. You'll want to know that."
patches.replace: "Twelve packets of redbark crossed Shilak in my pack," she said. "Nine came through sound. They're in Ranu. You'll want to know that."

open_errors.issue: In ch28 Meera tore the middleman page (ten winters of drop dates and crate marks) out of the count and gave it to Asha. At the Fair it is presented as part of the count, and the page is never returned.
open_errors.fix: Have Asha lay the torn page beside the count while she testifies.

patches.find: I have the weeks written, and the runner's name, a thin man with a bad left foot.
patches.replace: I have the weeks written, and the runner's name, a thin man with a bad left foot." She drew a folded page from her sleeve and laid it beside the count. "That's the guide's page back, torn from her book, and every date on it matches mine.

open_errors.issue: Coming down from the Saddle, they see the cairn 'beyond' Kothi Shilak. The Shilak Cairn stands above the village, between it and the pass: in ch3 it is reached up the gully, and in ch32 the villagers come up to it.
open_errors.fix: Place the cairn on the near slope, between the travellers and the village.

patches.find: and beyond it the small grey ring of the cairn.
patches.replace: and between it and them, on the near slope, the small grey ring of the cairn.
